title: Answering what-questions with ei mitään
summary: In the taught negative object replies, mitään means anything within a negative statement: En juo mitään (“I am not drinking anything”). Mitä sinä juot? — En juo mitään.
objectives: Answer an object what-question with nothing.
Use mitään with the appropriate negative verb in a full reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.

In the taught negative object replies, mitään means anything within a negative statement: En juo mitään (“I am not drinking anything”). Ei mitään is a natural short reply meaning nothing. Mitään is the partitive form of mikään.
keyPoints: Distinguish no thing from no person when answering the question.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: A full reply keeps the negative verb appropriate to its subject: en, ei, emme or eivät, followed by the negative main-verb form and mitään. Do not use nobody's subject word kukaan as the object of these actions.
A natural short reply to “Mitä sinä juot?” is “Ei mitään.” (“Nothing.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use mitään as the object in these negative replies, and retain the appropriate negative verb.

steps: Mitä: what; object question (asks what the action concerns). Mitä is the partitive form of mikä; its use follows the taught object or substance pattern.
sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
juot: you drink; verb (the action or state). Juo- + singular second-person -t gives juot.
En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.

juo: drink; main verb after the negative verb. Juoda removes -da to form juo. This is the singular third-person affirmative form and, after a negative verb, the negative main-verb form; the long vowel does not lengthen further.
